query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific grain refinement through severe plastic deformation can improve the dynamic strength-ductility performance of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline high-entropy alloy with coarse grain structure
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation via high-pressure torsion
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain size and increased dislocation density
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and dislocation hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in dynamic strength and 15% improvement in ductility compared to the untreated baseline
generation.baseline: Coarse-grained high-entropy alloy without severe plastic deformation
generation.boundary: Applicable to high-entropy alloys with face-centered cubic crystal structure, limited to room temperature and high strain rate conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the dynamic strength-ductility performance of high-entropy alloys with and without severe plastic deformation via high-pressure torsion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the severely deformed alloy does not exhibit a significant improvement in dynamic strength-ductility performance compared to the untreated baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
